claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children under 16, or are you responsible for any children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?** If so, could you tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's helpful. Now, let me ask you a few questions about your situation with Alex.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't actually - I'm living abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's an important detail.

**Which country are you currently living in?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Thank you for clarifying that.

**Are you a Crown servant (such as a civil servant, diplomat, or member of the armed forces posted abroad), or do you have any other special employment status that might affect your eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that - just a regular person living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

**Do you have the right to reside in Spain, or do you have British citizenship?** This will help me understand your immigration status and how it might affect your eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Based on what you've told me so far, I need to let you know about the rules for Child Benefit when living abroad.

According to the UK government rules, **you may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant**. However, you've indicated you're not a Crown servant and you're living in Spain.

The rules state that Child Benefit eligibility for those living abroad depends on specific circumstances and countries. Since you're living in Spain and are not a Crown servant, this falls outside the standard eligibility criteria I have available.

**I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office directly** to discuss your specific situation, as they can provide detailed guidance on whether your particular circumstances in Spain qualify you for Child Benefit. They'll be able to consider any bilateral agreements or specific arrangements that might apply to your situation.

Is there anything else about your circumstances in Spain that might be relevant - for example, are you working there, or do you have any other connection to the UK that might affect your eligibility?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing else really - I'm just living and working there normally. So does that mean I'm not eligible then?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided and the Child Benefit rules available to me, I need to give you a clear answer.

The UK government's Child Benefit eligibility rules state that you normally qualify if you're responsible for a child under 16 and **you live in the UK**. The rules do allow for some exceptions for people living abroad, specifically for Crown servants or in certain other circumstances, but these don't appear to apply to your situation.

Since you are:
- Living abroad in Spain
- Not a Crown servant
- Working normally there (not in a special employment status)

**You would not be eligible for Child Benefit under the standard rules.**

However, I would still recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office directly to confirm this, as there may be specific circumstances or agreements I'm not aware of that could affect your eligibility. They can give you definitive guidance on your particular situation.

Would you like me to provide you with the contact details for the Child Benefit Office, or is there anything else I can help clarify about the eligibility rules?

Since you are currently living in Spain and are not a Crown servant, you do not meet the standard eligibility criteria, which requires living in the UK.

**My recommendation:**
I would still advise you to contact the Child Benefit Office directly to discuss your situation in more detail, as they may be able to advise you on any special arrangements or if your circumstances change in the future.

Best of luck with your situation!
